Theme portrait · research pilot [scope-97]

Portrait: pastel

What makes Pastel Pastel, drawn on the package's real stylesheets and components and fixed to this theme. Every word, role and verb comes from themes/pastel/signature.json, and every claim there cites the token, selector or keyframes that proves it; tests/theme-portraits.spec.mjs refuses a citation the stylesheet does not contain. Each of the nine sections is a block with its own verdict. A row or verb marked Open is a proposal for Kenny, not a fact about the theme.

1 · Idea

Look at: the idea is at most three sentences, and the list under it is what may not move. Read each claim against the rest of this page: every later section should be explainable from these lines, and a claim that nothing below shows is a claim to strike. Each claim carries its proof, the token, selector or keyframes in pastel's own files that make it true.

Risograph printing: a lavender-milk ground, plum ink and the slight misregistration of a second pass. Soft without being weak, the inks are saturated and only the ground is pale, and every corner is round. Things behave like stickers, a flat shadow beside them, a small lift askew under the pointer, pressed flat, and move with a springy overshoot nothing else in the package has.

  1. The ground is tinted, not white: a lavender so pale it reads as white until white is put beside it.

    Proof
    • themes/pastel/tokens.json --background
    • themes/pastel/tokens.json --card

  2. Plum acts; mint and violet are fills, never actions.

  3. The overprint: the headline carries a second-pass duplicate held 2px off register.

    Proof

  4. Soft geometry: the largest radii in the package, and a rounded clip on the hero.

  5. The springy overshoot drives every arrival, fill, lift and press.

2 · Colour in its role

Look at: 12 roles, each a swatch of its token as the page resolves it, what the role may carry, what it may never carry, and a live component using it. The swatch and the component must show the same colour. Then read across the cards: a colour that appears in a component under a role it is told never to take is a finding. Roles in pastel: Milk, Paper, Plum ink, Rose plum, Mint, Mint ink, Violet, Sky, Boundary, Danger, Stamp plate, Second pass.

4 · Shape

Look at: the corners, the edges and what floats. Radius, borders, shadows, and last the one shape this theme is recognised by. Every example is the component as it ships; check that its corner, edge and shadow are the ones the sentence above it describes, at this zoom and at 200 %.

Radius

1rem by token; the register goes further: cards 1.2rem, panels 1.1rem, buttons 0.85rem, fields 0.65rem, badges 0.5rem, and the progress bar and the band are pills.

6 · Motion

Look at: first the live copies above the stage. Each verb has a Replay button that plays the register's own rule on a real component: hover and press are the register's :hover and :active rules applied by the page, not a copy of them. Then switch Reduced motion on and replay each again: what is left must be exactly the column "Reduced motion" in the table. Flicker in pastel: not allowed, Soft is the point: nothing here loops or opposes its own direction, and the spring is the only drama. Marked open, a proposal rather than a fact: attention.
For every copy below

Follows your system setting until you press it; the page rewrites its own motion guards, so the stylesheets decide what remains.

Look at: the ornaments drawn live: Pearls, The overprint, The sticker, The stamp, The rounded hero, The pill band, Halftone. Each must look like the sentence beside it, and none may compete with the content it decorates. An ornament a new component could reuse is the first thing to reach for in the recipe.

8 · Voice

Look at: how pastel talks: its case, the small words and prefixes it puts in front of things, how it draws instead of using icons, and what it never does. The sample under the list is real markup; every rule in the list should be visible in it.
Case
Sentence case everywhere; spaced mono capitals only for the microlabel, the brand tag, the stamp and footer headings.
Labels
  • A microlabel is a plum mono tick in spaced capitals.
  • A field label is the ink at weight 600, with no prefix.
  • A dropdown link carries a small ' ▾'.
  • The stamp swaps its word when the file is opened (the consumer's label and label-open).
Icons
Type does the work: a ' ▾' after a dropdown link, round status dots, no drawn glyphs of its own.
Never
  • The overprint on running text.
  • More than three inks at once.
  • Lose the tinted ground.
  • A redaction left covered on a page with no script.
  • A sharp corner or a flicker.

Worked example: a banner that asks for attention

A banner that asks for attention, from existing parts only: a white card with a plum mono tick, the destructive alert whose word 'Warning:' carries the meaning, the key phrase filled in mint, the plum sticker button beside the ghost one, and a string of pearls under it.
